articles.author: Edy Cu
articles.description:
A car brakes from 49 km/h to a stop. The instrument cluster keeps showing 48.
The renderer process is running. If you watch its liveness tick, it may still be ticking. If you ask it what it drew, it says the right number. Every check that lives inside or beside the renderer comes back green, and the driver is looking at a number that stopped being true seconds ago.
That is the gap I built Telltale to close: a watchdog proves the renderer is alive; only reading the glass back proves it tells the truth. Telltale is a separate QNX 8.0 process that reads back the pixels QNX Screen actually composed, decodes the speed digits, six warning lamps and a liveness tick, and compares them with the vehicle state. When the glass lies, it puts the true speed on screen first and deals with the renderer se…
articles.title: A heartbeat can't tell you the speedometer is lying: reading the glass back on QNX 8.0

articles.author: Lorenzo Fazioli
articles.description:
Wireshark per l'analisi difensiva


Wireshark trasforma il traffico di rete in dati osservabili. È utile per diagnosticare timeout, configurazioni DNS errate, certificati non validi e comunicazioni anomale, ma va usato solo su reti proprie o per le quali si ha autorizzazione esplicita.
Definisci obiettivo, perimetro e finestra temporale.
Usa una cattura limitata e scarta i dati sensibili.
Verifica la policy aziendale e le normative applicabili.
Evita password, sessioni e dati personali nei pacchetti esportati.
Iniziare con una cattura breve, poi isolare il problema con filtri di visualizzazione:
# Solo traffico verso o da un host
ip.addr == 192.0.2.10

# DNS
udp.port == 53 || tcp.port == 53

# Traffico HTTP non cifrato
http

# Handshake e problemi TCP
tcp.flags.syn == 1 || tcp.analysis.retransmission

In ambiente di laboratorio usa indirizzi di esempio come 192.0.2.10. Quando possibile, concentrati su handshake TLS, restituzioni DNS, risposte HTTP, retransmission e reset.
Riproduci il problema una sola volta.
Filtra il traffico pertinente.
Segui il flusso TCP o il stream HTTP.
Cerca risposte anomale, ritardi o protocolli inattesi.
Correla la cattura con log dell'applicazione e dell'infrastruttura.
Conserva solo il minimo necessario, con regole di retention.
Catturare tutto senza limitazioni.
Interpretare un pacchetto isolato come prova conclusiva.
Condividere .pcap contenenti credenziali o dati cliente.
Confondere strumenti di osservazione con strumenti di intrusione.
[ ] Autorizzazione documentata
[ ] Ambito e durata definita
[ ] Dati sensibili esclusi o anonimizzati
[ ] Correlazione con log
[ ] Evidenze salvate in modo controllato
[ ] Incidenti segnalati tramite i canali appropriati
Usare Wireshark significa capire cosa comunica un sistema. La parte più importante resta l'autorizzazione e la protezione dei dati catturati.
articles.title: Wireshark per l'analisi difensiva: leggere il traffico senza indovinare

PDF.js viewer pages need origin-aware inventory, not a library version claim


PDF.js is often embedded as a viewer in another application. The page may show a PDF title, a toolbar, or a document URL without identifying the JavaScript library that renders it. A public count of viewer pages can help a document-platform owner find the right assets, but the origin and embedding context matter more than the library name.
The fixed measurement on November 23, 2026 returned zero matches for app="PDF.js", 431 for title="PDF.js", and 2,530 for http.body="PDF.js viewer". The scope was sub_type=all, page 1, page size 1. These are index matches, not confirmed vulnerable viewer instances.
The PDF.js FAQ says the viewer runs with the permissions of ordinary JavaScript and follows the browser's same-ori…

articles.author: Prachit Parikh
articles.description:
Picture a sales director typing into the new AI data assistant on a Monday morning: "What was revenue last month?" A number comes back in four seconds. $8,550. Clean, confident, no caveats. She pastes it into a deck for the 10 AM leadership call.
Finance's number for the same month is $5,550.
Nobody wrote bad SQL. The agent's query ran. It joined nothing it shouldn't have, and it didn't make up a table. It picked one reasonable reading of "revenue last month" out of at least five, and it didn't tell anyone it had picked. In the fixture below, those five readings range from $5,550 to $8,550, a 54% spread on a ten-row table.
That's the failure I think BAs should be writing requirements for right now. A text-to-SQL agent rarely fails by writing broken SQL. It fails by writing correct SQL for …
articles.title: Text-to-SQL answer receipts: the spec I'd write before an AI agent answers one data question
